County the Metropolitan Districts Must File Annual Report With Douglas County

sources.text: Recycling Right -- 1 of 13 -- Recycling Guidelines  Waste Connections uses a single stream recycling model.  All acceptable recycling materials can be placed in one container  No sorting required. -- 2 of 13 -- -- 3 of 13 -- Non-Recyclable Items  Chip Bags  Candy Wrappers  Napkins  Paper Plates  Tissues  Pizza Boxes  Plastic Grocery Bags -- 4 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes?  From your home to the Recycling Center.  From the Recycling Center to the Manufacture.  From the Manufacture back to you. -- 5 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes  Once your recycle has been cleaned and sorted inside your home and placed in your recycle container it is picked up by a Waste Connections recycle Truck and heads to EcoCycle. When the truck reaches EcoCycle it is put on a large conveyer belt and the sorting process starts. Plastic, paper products, metal and glass are sorted from each other. Once all the plastics have been sorted together, they are then sorted again by type. Plastic bottles used for water and soda go one way and milk containers go in another and so forth. This is done for paper, glass and metal as well. Once everything has been sorted, the different types of materials are bundled together in big cubs at a certain weight and are ready to be sold and shipped.  The cleaner the materials are the better. This allows for fewer issues with the sorting equipment and a better price. One contaminated recycle container can cause the entire truck load of material to be deemed contaminated and sends the entire load to the landfill.

sources.text: According to the EPA, here are the environmental and economic benefits of using landfill gas:  ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a safe and renewable energy source.  Using landfill gas reduces the need to use more polluting forms of energy.  Using landfill gas reduces health and community risks, such as air pollution.  Landfills that use their landfill gas tend to be better managed and make better neighbors. -- 9 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit BENEFITS  ECONOMIC BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a cost-effective, reliable, and local source of energy.  Using landfill gas can generate economic benefits for the community.  Developing and maintaining a landfill gas energy project creates local jobs.  A landfill with good power potential can attract business to the community. -- 10 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  According to the EPA, “When municipal solid waste is first deposited in a landfill, it undergoes an aerobic (with oxygen) decomposition stage when little methane is generated. Then, typically within less than 1 year, anaerobic conditions are established and methane-producing bacteria begin to decompose the waste and generate methane.  Landfill gas (LFG) is a natural byproduct of the decomposition of organic material in landfills. LFG is composed of roughly 50 percent methane (the primary component of natural gas), 50 percent carbon dioxide (CO2) and a small amount of non-methane organic compounds. -- 11 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  CONVERTING LANDFILL GAS TO ENERGY  Instead of escaping into the air, LFG can be captured, converted, and used as an energy source.

This system directs the collected gas to a central point where it can be transported, compressed, and filtered before it is combusted to generate electricity. -- 12 of 13 -- In Conclusion  Recycling right is the best way for Americans to protect the environment and stimulate the economy.  Recycling saves resource and reduces pollution.  Recycling is a shared responsibility.  Its easy! -- 13 of 13 --

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool.

sources.text: Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches. Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited. Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them from the pool. Personal sound equipment, such as stereos or wireless speakers, are permitted as long as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the pool. If any complaints are received, Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or upon repeated complaint, asked to turn off the device or leave the pool. The pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather events that present danger to Users.

sources.text: The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC . Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? The water rates are structured to recover system costs. Outdoor water rates were designed to encourage water-wise irrigation practices. Outdoor water use increases the demand on our water system, and therefore the operational costs of our facilities. Additionally, when water is used outdoors it is fully consumed and not returned to the system. Water How do I move into higher tiers each month? The first tier of fee rates per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100% of the customer’s water budget. The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer. Water used during the establishment period (45 days following the installation of turf and plant material) will be billed at the first tier fee rate, and will not count against the water budget. sources.text: Once the Siemens technician arrives at your home, the equipment upgrades should take approximately 2 hours. Water Communication Retrofit Will I be able to use internet while the upgrade is taking place? The technician will need to shut off a circuit breaker to perform the necessary electrical work. If your internet is utilizing that same circuit breaker, you will not be able to access the internet for approximately 45 minutes while electrical work is being performed. Because of this, we strongly recommend not scheduling critical tasks that will require internet access or VoIP phone use during your service window. Water Communication Retrofit What can I do to prepare? In order to minimize the time required, prior to the technician’s arrival please clear adequate space (at least 3 square feet) around your water meter panel, electrical breaker box, and STEWARD equipment. This equipment is typically located in the basement. If you do not have a basement, the equipment is typically located in the garage. Water Communication Retrofit What information should I be ready to share? If you have changed the default login to your CenturyLink ONT /modem’s admin portal, please be prepared to provide that information as well. If you would prefer not to share this information, please be prepared to input your credentials for the technician at the necessary times. If you do not know your STEWARD login credentials, visit the Lumiere website . Water Communication Retrofit Why are you removing the virtual private network (VPN) hardware? The virtual private network ( VPN ) hardware was previously necessary to ensure proper encryption of water meter information during transmission to the water billing system. This is no longer the case as we are now able to use an alternate encryption method.

sources.text: Application fees can be paid via check made payable to Sterling Ranch CAB, or via credit/debit card. Please contact the team at the Resident Resource Center for assistance paying via credit/debit card. Checks can be mailed or dropped off to Sterling Ranch CAB, 8220 Piney River Ave, Littleton, CO 80125. Design Review After I receive my approval, can I modify or deviate from my application slightly? Approval was granted based on the information the homeowner provided to the committee on the application. A new Design Review Application will need to be submitted should a homeowner need to make any changes to the original application. (EXCEPT for plant material selection as long as it is for water to water same) Design Review How long does the Design Review Process take? The Design Review Committee has up to 30 days to review a submittal from the date a completed submittal package was received at the Design Review Committee meeting. If you have not been notified in writing by the 31st day after the meeting, the submittal is deemed to be denied. It is the responsibility of the applicant to contact the Design Review Committee to determine the status of the submittal. Design Review How many days do I have to install my rear yard? The rear yard landscape must be completed within 120 days following your closing. A Winter Deferral Period for completion of rear yard planting is granted for closings from November 1 to April 30. Design Review Am I allowed to make changes to my grading or drainage? The DRC does not evaluate changes to grading or drainage. Applicants are to seek approval from the County and/or other appropriate governing bodies. The DRC is not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage while installing landscaping or other improvements.

Design Review Do I need Design Review Committee approval for my fence installation? No, fences are installed on property lines and must meet the Sterling Ranch fence design specifications. A friendly reminder to always call 811 for a utilities/wire locate before ever digging for anything in your yard. Design Review Am I limited to the plants on the Pre-Approved Recommend Plant List? Sterling Ranch collaborated with Denver Botanic Gardens to research plantings that flourish in Colorado’s semi-arid climate. The concerted research effort trialed planting for water sustainability and resiliency and took form as a test garden planted on the property that was maintained and observed for three years. The recommend plant list is a great start to understanding the Sterling Ranch planting palette, but the Design Review Committee will review additional plant material requests. Design Review Am I limited to the landscape contractors on the Pre-Approved Landscaper List? No, you may work with a landscaper of your choice, but that professional landscaper will need to meet with our Architectural and Community Standards Director to become certified and approved. The approval process includes education on Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Design Review process. Please note, inclusion on this list does not constitute the CAB’s endorsement of any of these companies. This list is only intended to identify the individuals that have attended the CAB’s required informational sessions regarding the Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives.

Learn more about Design Review Compliance Are there any guidelines I need to follow to have a temporary dumpster or a storage pod at my house? Please submit an Application for General Architectural Improvements to the Design Review Committee for approval. Include with the application timeframe for dumpster or storage pod to be at property. Please note, dumpsters and storage pods must be placed in your driveway and are not allowed on a public right-of-way per Douglas County officials. Compliance What is the guideline for having a recreational vehicle at my home? The maximum amount of time a Recreational Vehicle is allowed to be parked is three overnights (e.g., 72 hours) during any 7-day period for loading, delivery, and maintenance. Periodic movement of the vehicle for the purpose of circumventing this standard shall not qualify the vehicle for an exception from this standard. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do I need to submit my paint colors even if I am painting my home the exact same colors? DRC approval is required, even if re-painting is being done with the same colors as the original or previous paint color. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do trampolines and play equipment require approval? DRC approval is required. Trampolines will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, setbacks from property lines, method of installation, and proposed safety netting. Trampolines are required to be anchored per manufacturer specifications.

sources.text: Compliance Is it okay for me to access the open space to do improvements on my property? No, all access to your property must be from the street side at the front of your home. Accessing the property through another lot, open space, parks, or landscaped tracts is prohibited. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Section IV. Landscaping Standards. Compliance What can I do about a barking dog or a neighbor that does not clean up after their animals on a regular basis? If you are trying to solve a problem with a barking dog or clean up after a pet, please start with communicating your concern to the pet owner or contact the following county authorities: Douglas County Animal Services, 303-660-7529, 7:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m. Sheriff’s Department Dispatch, 303-660-7500 (After 6 p.m. if an animal problem requires immediate attention). Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool.

sources.text: White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool. Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches.

sources.text: Sterling Ranch Code of Rules May 25, 2023 {00488209} Page 65 Registrations may be granted via reciprocity to individuals who hold registrations in other Colorado municipalities, on a case-by-case basis, as deemed appropriate by the Community Authority Board (“CAB”). AN APPLICANT MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT HE/SHE MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS BY PROVIDING CURRENT PROOF OF PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS. IN THE ABSENCE OF THESE CREDENTIALS, AN APPLICANT MAY SUBMIT A NARRATIVE LISTING THREE MOST RECENT PROJECTS, DOLLAR AMOUNT, COMPLETION DATE, AND CONTACT INFORMATION FOR THE PERSON FOR WHOM THE PROJECT WAS DONE. The CAB reserves the right to deny, suspend, or revoke any registration in accordance with its policies. ATTACHMENT G APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL OF LANDSCAPE PROFESSIONALS Registration requirements apply companies or organizations, not to individuals. The registered company or organization is responsible for all work performed under its supervision. Colorado law governs the sizes and types of projects that unlicensed individuals can design, and is independent from CAB policies. Registrations are valid for a period of three (3) years. Registration renewals for professionals in good standing may be issued upon receipt of acknowledgment of revisions to policies, criteria, or other applicable codes. Non-compliance with these policies may deem an applicant ineligible for renewal or result in an applicant’s removal from the approval list.

Pet mesh screen is required to be 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh used on the inside of the fence, not to exceed the top rail in height, and continued down to ground level. . Covers (ex: tarps, sheets, blankets, etc.) are NOT allowed. Kennel . A free-standing panel-system kennel may not exceed 50 square feet and must be a maximum of 48 inches in height. .

sources.text: The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants. Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com LANDSCAPE SCREENS DRC approval is required for landscape screens and will be considered based on the location of the screens, the size of your yard and the impact of screens on neighbors and the community. . 5’ maximum overall height for exposed landscape screen from grade. If plantings are installed at the base of the screen, facing out toward the community view, screen height will be allowed at a 6’ maximum overall height from grade. . 8’ maximum overall width for landscape screens. Multiple screens may not be attached at corners, at edges, to sheds, or to the house. Must be freestanding in the rear or side yard. . Landscape screens are only allowed in rear or side yards and are not allowed in easements. A maximum of three (3) screens are allowed if lot square footage permits. The DRC will review on a case by case basis. . Landscape screens must have 30% required transparency. . Materials must be constructed of a minimum 50% top grade redwood or cedar, or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home. If other materials like masonry or metal are used, they must match the architectural style of the house. Vinyl is not permitted. . Landscape screens may be either painted or stained. Paint colors must match or compliment house colors. Stain must match fence stain (Sherwin Williams #3002 Belvedere Tan) or a natural stain. Wood grain is allowed to show through. . Landscape screens may be used to screen hot tub areas on two sides only. .

Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com 3-RAIL FENCING SPECIFICATIONS Homeowners are responsible for installation of side and rear yard fencing. Fencing is to be placed on property lines unless otherwise approved by DRC. Please note, single-family detached homes are not required to have fencing between homes. Any fence type request that varies from the Standards described in the Residential Property Owner Guidebook requires DRC approval. TYPICAL SPECIFICATIONS: SINGLE FAMILY HOMES (Does NOT include Lennar Elements homes in Providence Village) Two fence styles are approved for use on interior lot lines between homes: . 3-rail cedar dimensional lumber fence stained in the approved color, Sherwin Williams #3002 “Belvedere Tan” or . An open-rail fence consisting of 3 concrete rails and concrete vertical posts per community specifications (can be downloaded at www.sterlingranchcab.com) with integral coloring in Solomon #338 “Earthen.” . All interior lot line fencing must be stained and kept in good repair. ADDITIONAL GATES Requests will only be considered for additional gates located within front wing fencing, interior lot line fencing between two homes if both neighbors are in agreement, signatures required on submittal plan drawings, or rear perimeter fencing when adjacent to CAB owned common space with CAB permission. Additional gates within side and rear property line concrete fencing that are street facing are not allowed.

Stored within property boundaries so as not to be in the right-of-way which includes the sidewalk and tree lawn . Dumpsters are only allowed during construction, remodeling, and moving. If it is determined the dumpster is not necessary, or that the construction, remodeling, or moving is not proceeding in a diligent manner, then the dumpster will need to be removed . Dumpsters must be emptied regularly so unsightly debris does not exceed top edge of dumpster and to prevent debris from flying out . Application for Improvement must be submitted via submit@sterlingranchdrc.com with the location of the roll-off container and the time frame the container will be on the property . Temporary moving containers and portable storage “PODS” are permitted for no more than fourteen (14) days. If needed for longer an Application for General Architectural Improvement must be submitted for DRC review and approval. . Property owners should contact Douglas County for any additional permit or engineering requirements. All roll-off containers are required to be placed within property boundaries and are not allowed in the right-of-way, including the sidewalk or tree lawns. Temporary fencing is not permitted. sources.text: If you haven’t signed up to get access to the Overlook Clubhouse, complete the Resident Amenity Form online today! **For homeowners who registered for the Overlook Clubhouse prior to its opening in October 2020 should have received the email to complete account setup already. If you have not received the email or your link is expired, please contact the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com and a staff member will assist you.** This account and password are for the new CIVICREC system and will be used for registering for events, reserving time to use the fitness center, purchasing fitness classes, additional guest passes, and more! Follow the instructions listed below to complete your account setup. How to Finish Your Online Account Setup Open the email. You will have a username (your email provided) and a temporary password to log in. Select TO LOGIN AND CHANGE YOUR PASSWORD NOW CLICK HERE. You will be redirected to the new CIVICREC Website. Once logged in, select ACCOUNT in the top lefthand corner. Select the pencil icon next to your name. In the lower-left corner, select RESET CIVICREC PASSWORD. You will be prompted to confirm that you would like to reset the password. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Follow the instructions to reset your password. Registering for Events & Programs Navigate to the Community Calendar . Click on the event that interests you. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts.

Home - FAQs How do I trouble shoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Home - FAQs Home - FAQs 6 How do I submit an application for Design Review? sources.title: Pickleball Courts
sources.text: Pickleball Courts Pickleball Facility Guidelines Hours and Reservations Hours: Weekdays 7 am-dusk; Weekends 8 am-dusk. Courts are located at Sterling Ranch Ave. and Middle Fork St. Free street parking is available near the courts. No pets are allowed inside the courts. Courts are available for reservations and drop-in play. Courts opened for play on August 1, 2025. Court reservations can be made for a maximum of two hours/day via the Sterling Ranch CAB CourtReserve portal or CourtReserve phone app. Residents can make reservations up to seven days in advance. Non-residents can make reservations up to three days in advance starting September 1, 2025. Residents: Free Non-residents: $40/court for up to four players Open play for non-residents: $20 for two players. Open play hours: Mon-Fri: 7-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Sat-Sun: 8-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Reservation hours: Mon-Fri: 11 am-5 pm. Sat-Sun: 11 am-5 pm. Tournaments and lessons held by Sterling Ranch CAB take precedence. Court Reserve Court Reserve is a web-based pickleball court reservation application to make it easier for members to reserve pickleball courts, and register for open play from a web browser or phone app. Click here for details on setting up your account. General Information Follow USA Pickleball rules for behavior and etiquette. (Click here to view the rules.) Be courteous; all skill levels are welcome. Bring your own paddles and balls. Tennis or court shoes required. Courts are for pickleball only-no skateboards, bikes, pets, etc. Courts are for personal play only. Paid or private events are prohibited. CAB-organized recreational programming is allowed. No ball machines, generators, chairs, tables, or glass items on courts. Dispose of trash, avoid sitting or leaning on nets/posts. Courts may be slippery when wet.

sources.title: Annual Drinking Water Consumer Confidence Report Calendar Year 2021
sources.text: Annual Drinking Water Consumer Confidence Report: Calendar Year 2021 general information Dominion Water and Sanitation District (Dominion) is the whole sale water supplier to the CAB. Unlike other water providers, Dominion’s supply starts with renewable water. In 2021, Dominion received water through contracts with the City of Aurora. Water is diverted from the South Platte River at Strontia Springs Reservoir and then runs through the City of Aurora’s tunnel to the Rampart Reservoir and transmission pipelines to the Moore Water Treatment Plant. Once it reaches the treatment facility, a number of treatment processes are utilized including coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection. The sources of drinking water include lakes, rivers, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. In order to ensure that tap water is safe to drink, Colorado Department of Health and Environment (CDPHE) prescribes regulations limiting the amount of certain contaminants in water provided by public water systems. The sources of drinking water (both tap water and bottled water) include rivers, lakes, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. As water travels over the surface of the land or through the ground, it dissolves naturally occurring minerals and, in some cases, radioactive material, and can pick up substances resulting from the presence of animals or from human activity. Contaminants that may be present in source water include: . Microbial contaminants: viruses and bacteria that may come from sewage treatment plants, septic systems, agricultural livestock operations, and wildlife. . Inorganic contaminants: salts and metals, which can be naturallyoccurring or result from urban storm water runoff, industrial or domestic wastewater discharges, oil and gas production, mining, or farming. . Pesticides and herbicides: may come from a variety of sources, such as agriculture, urban storm water runoff, and residential uses. . Radioactive contaminants: can be naturally occurring or be the result of oil and gas production and mining activities. . Organic chemical contaminants: including synthetic and volatile organic chemicals, which are byproducts of industrial processes and petroleum production, and also may come from gas stations, urban storm water runoff, and septic systems.

Lead in Drinking Water If present, elevated levels of lead can cause serious health problems (especially for pregnant women and young children). It is possible that lead levels at your home may be higher than other homes in the community as a result of materials used in your home’s plumbing. If you are concerned about lead in your water, you may wish to have your water tested. When your water has been sitting for several hours, you can minimize the potential for lead exposure by flushing your tap for 30 seconds to 2 minutes before using water for drinking or cooking. Additional information on lead in drinking water, testing methods, and steps you can take to minimize exposure is available from the Safe Drinking Water Hotline (1-800-426-4791) or at epa.gov/safewater/lead. sources.text: Q: Is the CAB certified to inspect the streets and other areas that they build and does Douglas County recognize our inspections? A: Inspections are carried out by both CAB personnel and Douglas County. Each entity inspects for different reasons. The CAB inspects the public infrastructure that will be owned and maintained by the CAB, for example, the water and sewer mainlines. Both the CAB team and Douglas County inspectors inspect street, curb, gutter, and sidewalk improvements that will be accepted by the County. The CAB inspects to ensure the improvements are completed to contract specification, which includes County specifications. The County inspection is additional as they are certifying their acceptance of those elements as the County has long term operations and maintenance responsibility. Q: When can we look forward to seeing Burns Park built? A: Civil construction and grading will begin in Filing 7A in early 2024. Filing 7A is the west boundary of Burns Park. As that work progresses and is completed, portions of Burns Park will begin to be constructed, starting in the southern part of the park. Very shortly CAB will be asking Douglas County for $300,000 to start designing Burns Park as a "regional park.” Q: If we have another area of homes open for development, and we need bonds to fund construction, when do those bonds need to be paid and who pays for them? A: The CAB will issue bonds to support public infrastructure construction in the new areas. That area will be part of Metropolitan District 4 Subdistrict A. CAB will issue Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds that are supported by future property tax revenues in the Subdistrict.

sources.text: As with other parts of the community, payment of those bonds is subject to the 50 mils (as adjusted) debt service mill levy cap and counts towards the total community debt limit of $1,800,000,000. Those bonds are payable only by the properties in District 4 Subdistrict-A. Other CAB debt, specifically the Jr. Subordinate bonds, are supported by the pledge of revenues from all Sterling Ranch Metropolitan Districts and pay for costs that the CAB was not able to cover at the time of construction but that benefit the entire Sterling Ranch community. -- 27 of 29 -- Q: How many schools will we have? A: Douglas County School District will continue to monitor community growth and will determine ultimately how many schools will be in Sterling Ranch. Both CAB and the School District recognize the immediate need for an elementary school here in Sterling Ranch. As many of you are aware, the most recent School District capital improvement bonds to build schools failed. Therefore, the School District doesn’t currently have the funds to build a school here in Sterling Ranch. However, there are a other options that may expedite school construction such as a charter school. Q: Who ends up paying for the bonds? A: Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds are issued by the CAB and paid for through property taxes pledged by respective districts. All debt service payments are subject to the mill levy cap and total debt issuance limitation. Q: If we can issue up to $1.8B with 12,000 homes, with interest, how much will I as an individual owner wind up paying? A: The debt authorization limit includes debt beyond the initial buildout of the community to account for refunding, refinancing, or future capital development needs.

sources.text: You’ll never pay more than the 50 mil debt service cap, as adjusted, through your taxes. What will you pay over the life of living in your home? That’s open to many different factors, including the value of your home, the length of time you live in the community, impact of future bond refunding’s and future market conditions. The bonds are paid off over 30- or 40-year increments, and the benefit of funding infrastructure through bonds is that future residents pay for the costs of improvements as well as current residents, ensuring greater equity over time. Q: Can the CAB issue bonds without an election? A: There is not a requirement for a general election prior to debt issuance. The CAB, through the Districts, has debt authorization and pledge agreements that support debt issuance. Residents elect members to serve on the Metropolitan District Boards and the District Boards appoint members to the CAB Board. Q: Regarding the school parcels, are those currently owned by Douglas County or is that land sold by the development company? A: During the land planning process, a certain amount of land is determined to be used for open space, residential, commercial, and for schools. The County requires a certain dedications at certain population thresholds. As areas of the development are platted, land is dedicated to Douglas County for specific uses, like a library or schools. The land is not sold to the County. Q: Can you talk about all the other expenses that we pay as owners, water is expensive, trash, streetlights? -- 28 of 29 -- A: Costs for these items are based on expenses. For example, the Waste Connections contract has a built-in year over year increase, and that increase is passed on to the owners for the cost of the contract. Streetlights are very similar.

sources.text: Water Billing & Payment Options USPS Mail Pay by Check or Money Order - Send a check to the billing mailing address. All checks must be made payable to "American Conservation and Billing Solutions", P.O. Box 51280, Colorado Springs, CO 80949 Please remember to write your account number on your check . Payment Options: Please register your account through Utility Hawk ( https://srcab.utilityhawk.us ) or through the AmCoBi website: Point your Web browser to: http://www.amcobi.com/pay-online Select the "Pay Online" link on the home page. Follow the instructions. Your online account allows you to choose the best payment options for you, check your account balance and activity, and elect to receive your water bill electronically (eBill). AmCoBi's ePay service allows you to pay your bill online with an automatic withdrawal from your checking/savings account (ACH) free of charge. You can also use a debit or credit card with a processing fee of 2.95%, charged by Paymentus, the payment processing provider. Other Payment Options: Bank Bill Pay - please make sure to update your bank bill pay with your new AMCoBi account number and remittance address to ensure proper delivery. Pay by Phone at 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 Pay by Email or Text by replying to the received message from the Payment Portal. Instant Payment Options: Instant pay allows you to make a payment that AmCoBi will receive instantly using VISA, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, PayPal, Venmo, Amazon Pay, or Walmart Bill Pay. Questions? For questions about your account and general assistance, please contact the Client Care Team at AmCoBi. The AmCoBi, Colorado-based Client Care Team, will answer questions or assist with any issues that arise. They are available Monday - Friday, from 8:00 am - 5:00 pm MST. Contact them by phone or e-mail: Toll-free: 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 E-mail: ClientCare@AmCoBi.com Contact Us Resident Resource Center info@sterlingranchcab.com Physical Address 8220 Piney River Avenue Sterling Ranch , CO 80125 Phone: 720-661-9694 Emergency Phone: 720-661-9694 Ext. 2

sources.text: Understanding Your Water Bill Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer service after closing on their homes. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. American Conservation and Billing Solutions ( AmCoBi) administer the monthly water bill each month. Sterling Ranch uses a tiered water rate structure for billing. This tiered water rate structure encourages water-smart usage both inside and out. sources.title: Pickleball Courts
sources.text: The pickleball courts are open weekdays from 7 a.m. to dusk and weekends from 8 a.m. to dusk. The courts are at Sterling Ranch Avenue and Middle Fork Street. Free street parking is available nearby, and pets are not allowed inside the courts. The courts allow reservations and drop-in play. Court reservations are limited to two hours per day through CourtReserve. Residents can reserve up to seven days in advance. Nonresidents can reserve up to three days in advance. Pickleball is free for residents. The nonresident price is $40 per court for up to four players, or $20 for two nonresident players during open play. Open play is Monday through Friday from 7–11 a.m. and 5–8 p.m., and Saturday and Sunday from 8–11 a.m. and 5–8 p.m. Reservation hours are 11 a.m.–5 p.m. every day. Sterling Ranch CAB tournaments and lessons take precedence over ordinary play. Players must bring their own paddles and balls and wear tennis or court shoes. The courts are for pickleball and personal play only. Paid or private events are prohibited. Bikes, skateboards, pets, ball machines, generators, chairs, tables, and glass items are not allowed on the courts. Courts may be slippery when wet. Snow shoveling is prohibited, and gates are locked when the courts are snow-covered. Children under 13 must have a Sterling Ranch resident age 16 or older present. When courts are full, games are limited to 11 points and players rotate using the paddle rack. Groups of four take priority, and challenge play is not allowed while others are waiting. For pickleball-court questions, call Sterling Ranch CAB at 720-728-7257.

sources.title: 2026 Annual Drinking Water Quality Report (2025 data)
sources.text: The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board has compiled its 2026 Annual Drinking Water Quality Report. This includes the Sterling Ranch Consumer Confidence Report (CCR), the CCR from Dominion Water & Sanitation District, and the CCRs from their water sources. This report details water quality data for the 2025 calendar year. STERLING RANCH CAB, PWS ID: CO0118724 2026 CCR Page 7 of 8 Description: The hydrant located at 8738 Animas River Street experienced a positive coliform result. The hydrant was flushed for several minutes, the chlorine residual was tested, and a 2nd (repeat) coliform sample was collected. The 2nd sample also tested positive for total coliform. Action Taken: All of the water main valves in the area were checked to ensure that they were in the correct position. The hydrant was flushed, chlorine residual tested and another total coliform sample was collected on January 15th, 2025. The result was “absent” of coliform and e-coli. STERLING RANCH CAB, PWS ID: CO0118724 2026 CCR Page 8 of 8 Name Description Time Period Describe the steps taken to resolve and the anticipated resolution date: CROSS CONNECTION RULE FAILURE TO MEET CROSS CONNECTION CONTROL AND/OR BACKFLOW PREVENTION REQUIREMENTS - M610 12/17/2024 - 04/15/2025 This was resolved on April 22, 2025, when the CDPHE confirmed that our Backflow Program was reviewed and approved. IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR DRINKING WATER Dominion Water and Sanitation District Had the following Violations Identified During a Drinking Water Inspection Este informe contiene información muy importante sobre su agua potable. Tradúzcalo o hable con alguien que lo entienda bien. Our water system recently violated a drinking water requirement. Although this situation is not an emergency, as our customers you have a right to know what happened, what you should do, and what we are doing to correct this situation. A routine drinking water inspection conducted on 2/13/2026 by the state drinking water program identified the following violations that may pose a risk to public health. Identified Violation Required Language Date Correction is Required Steps We Are Taking F325 - Monitoring and Reporting N/A July 11, 2026 Dominion WSD Submitted documentation of periodic inspections conducted on March 27th, 2026 to the State. Dominion WSD developed a detailed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for tank inspections and submitted it to the State. Dominion WSD developed and implemented a three-step process to schedule, execute and document all future tank inspections to ensure they are conducted and documented. This documentation was all submitted to the state and resolved the violation on 4/24/2026. M613 - Monitoring and Reporting N/A July 11, 2026 Dominion WSD submitted the Annual Backflow Report for 2025 and resolved the violation on 2/13/2026. Violations, Significant Deficiencies and Formal Enforcement Actions TWO VIOLATIONS: FAILURE TO MONITOR AND/OR REPORT Non-Health-Based Violations These violations do not usually mean that there was a problem with the water quality. If there had been, Castle Rock Water would have notified customers immediately. Castle Rock Water missed collecting a sample (water quality is unknown), and reported the sample result after the due date, or a completed report/notice was not received by the required date. Please share this information with all the other people who drink this water, especially those who may not have received this notice directly (for example, people in apartments, nursing homes, schools, and businesses). This can be done by posting this notice in a public place or distributing copies by hand or mail. Violation #1 Name Description Time Period CHLORINE/ CHLORAMINE FAILURE TO MONITOR AND/OR REPORT 05/01/2025 - 05/31/2025 Finally, Castle Rock Water experienced the failure of this instrument twice within the span of one week, of which this failure was the first. Although the instrument was successfully restarted on May 24, the faulty instrument was not replaced until June 1. Castle Rock Water added a redundant monitoring instrument on 6/6/2025, to prevent this situation from ever reoccurring. Violation #2 Name Description Time Period CHLORINE/ CHLORAMINE FAILURE TO MONITOR AND/OR REPORT 06/01/2025 - 06/30/2025 Describe the steps taken to resolve and the anticipated resolution date: Our water system missed a drinking water monitoring requirement. Although this situation was not an emergency, as you have a right to know what happened, what you should do, and what we did to correct this situation. We are required to continuously monitor our drinking water at the entry point of the distribution system for residual disinfectant concentration at the Plum Creek Water Purification Facility. While Castle Rock Water has multiple ways to monitor the disinfectant concentration, an entry point monitoring instrument officially designated by the State records results on four-hour intervals to ensure that this concentration is never less than the regulatory requirement. The results of this regular monitoring are used to make sure our drinking water meets regulatory standards.

sources.title: Memberships
sources.text: There is no additional cost for club memberships for Sterling Ranch residents. Once you close on your home in Sterling Ranch, complete the Resident Amenity Form . List each member of your household that lives in the house (including children). Memberships will not be given to family members not residing in the home. Proof of Sterling Ranch address will be required by all adults listed on the Resident Amenity Form that are 21 or older. Anyone 20 years of age or younger is not required proof of residency. Acceptable documentation includes closing documents, utility bills, driver's licenses, etc. You will receive a confirmation email when your membership cards are ready to be picked up from recreation@sterlingranchcab.com . Allow the Resident Services Team two business days to process your membership request and prepare your access cards. Each resident requires a membership card (or a picture of your card) to access the Clubhouse. If you have lost your card, you may purchase a new one for $5.00.

sources.title: Snow Removal
sources.text: Douglas County handles the public roadways throughout the community. The Community Authority Board (CAB) removes snow in common areas, trails, shared drives, and alley areas. Homeowners are responsible for snow removal from their sidewalks and driveways. Priority 1- The Overlook Clubhouse, CAB offices parking lots. Priority 2- Shared Drives, Alleys, and Mail Kiosks Priority 3- Peripheral sidewalks, parks, and areas with streets but no homes. Overlook Clubhouse - zero tolerance Sidewalks - 2" threshold Mail Kiosks - 2" threshold for priority removal. sources.title: Sterling Ranch 311
sources.text: Sterling Ranch residents can use Sterling Ranch 311 to submit service requests or feedback using their mobile devices and computers. Please be advised that this request service is for non-emergency service issues, comments, and concerns only. If you're experiencing an emergency, please dial 911. Choose a service request category from the drop-down menu that matches your request. Drag the map marker to the location of your issue or type in the exact address. Click "Confirm Location". Add a photo if available or click "No Photo". Enter a description and answer any related questions. Click "Confirm Details".

sources.title: Community Volunteers
sources.text: Our Ranch Hands pitch in to keep Sterling Ranch looking its best-whether it’s planting bulbs, raking leaves, or pulling those pesky weeds. Think of it as the summertime version of our Snow Angels program: instead of shovels, we bring out the rakes and gardening gloves to help those who cannot do this work themselves during a health crisis, family emergency, or other significant disruption in their life. These volunteers help clear sidewalks and driveways for those unable to shovel. Questions? Send us an email to get involved: info@sterlingranchcab.com Want to join the Navigators crew? Reach out to communitynavigators@sterlingranchcab.com

sources.title: Trash & Recycling
sources.text: For Providence, trash is picked up weekly on Monday, and recycling is picked up every other Monday. For Ascent, trash is picked up weekly on Tuesday, and recycling is picked up every other Tuesday. For Prospect and Parkvale, trash is picked up weekly on Thursday, and recycling is picked up every other Thursday. Make sure to place bins outside by 7 am for trash collection. Containers for pickup may be placed on the street or alleyway on the morning of pickup and must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the end of the pickup day. Trash pickup will be delayed by one day for the following holidays: New Year's Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Christmas

factLedger.displayValue: Violation #2 Name Description Time Period CHLORINE/ CHLORAMINE FAILURE TO MONITOR AND/OR REPORT 06/01/2025 - 06/30/2025 Describe the steps taken to resolve and the anticipated resolution date: Our water system missed a drinking water monitoring requirement. Although this situation was not an emergency, as you have a right to know what happened, what you should do, and what we did to correct this situation. We are required to continuously monitor our drinking water at the entry point of the distribution system for residual disinfectant concentration at the Plum Creek Water Purification Facility. While Castle Rock Water has multiple ways to monitor the disinfectant concentration, an entry point monitoring instrument officially designated by the State records results on four-hour intervals to ensure that this concentration is never less than the regulatory requirement. The results of this regular monitoring are used to make sure our drinking water meets regulatory standards.

factLedger.displayValue: Trash is collected every week: Monday in Providence, Tuesday in Ascent, and Thursday in Prospect and Parkvale. Recycling is picked up every other week on the same area day.
factLedger.normalizedValue: trash is collected every week: monday in providence, tuesday in ascent, and thursday in prospect and parkvale. recycling is picked up every other week on the same area day.
factLedger.supportingText: For Providence, trash is picked up weekly on Monday, and recycling is picked up every other Monday. For Ascent, trash is picked up weekly on Tuesday, and recycling is picked up every other Tuesday. For Prospect and Parkvale, trash is picked up weekly on Thursday, and recycling is picked up every other Thursday.

factLedger.displayValue: Put bins out by 7 a.m. and return them to a screened location by the end of pickup day.
factLedger.normalizedValue: put bins out by 7 a.m. and return them to a screened location by the end of pickup day.
factLedger.supportingText: Make sure to place bins outside by 7 am for trash collection. Containers for pickup may be placed on the street or alleyway on the morning of pickup and must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the end of the pickup day.

factLedger.displayValue: New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas move pickup back by one day.
factLedger.normalizedValue: new year’s day, memorial day, independence day, labor day, thanksgiving, and christmas move pickup back by one day.
factLedger.supportingText: Trash pickup will be delayed by one day for the following holidays: New Year's Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Christmas
